sourceFlowReconstruction: L1-7 MISHNAH: seven days before Yom Kippur they separate the Kohen Gadol from his house to the Parhedrin chamber and prepare another kohen in his place lest a disqualification befall him. R. Yehuda: also another wife is prepared lest his wife die, as it says 'vekhiper ba'ado uve'ad beito', 'beito' is his wife. They said to him: if so, there is no end to the matter. No decision between the views is stated.

L8-11 GEMARA cites 'tenan hatam': seven days before the burning of the parah they separated the kohen who burns it from his house to the chamber on the face of the Bira, north-east, called Lishkat Beit HaEven.
L12-14 Gemara's own question and answer: why that name? Because all its acts are in vessels of dung, stone and earth.

L14-20 'Mai taama': since a tevul yom is fit for the parah, as a Mishnah teaches (detenan): they would make the kohen who burns the parah tamei and immerse him, to remove [the view] from the heart of the Sadducees, who said it was done by those whose sun had set; the Rabbis instituted dung, stone and earth vessels, which do not receive tumah, so that it not be treated lightly.

L20-24 'Mai shena' north-east: since it is a chatat and a chatat requires north, and 'el nokhach penei ohel moed' is written of it, the Rabbis instituted a north-east chamber so that it have a heikera.

L24-27 'Mai bira': Rabba bar bar Chana in the name of R. Yochanan: a place on the Temple Mount named Bira. Reish Lakish: the whole Mikdash is called Bira, as it says 'habira asher hakhinoti'. Not resolved.

L27-31 'Mena hanei milei': R. Minyomi bar Chilkiya - R. Machseya bar Idi - R. Yochanan: 'ka'asher asa bayom hazeh tziva Hashem la'asot lekhaper aleikhem'; 'la'asot' = acts of the parah, 'lekhaper' = acts of Yom Kippur.
L32-34 Challenge: granted the whole verse cannot be about the parah, since 'lekhaper' is written and the parah is not for atonement; but say the whole verse is about Yom Kippur?
L34-38 'Amri': derive tziva-tziva; here 'tziva Hashem la'asot', there 'zot chukat hatorah asher tziva Hashem lemor'; as there parah so here parah; as here separation so there separation.

L39 'Ve'eima' - a further challenge only begins; nothing of it is stated on 2a. Open at the physical end of the daf: whether the tziva-tziva derivation survives that challenge; the Bira dispute; the Mishnah's dispute is undecided on the page.
dafSummaryEvidence: Every clause maps to L1-39: Mishnah L1-7; Parah citation and name L8-14; tevul yom, Sadducees, vessels L14-20; north-east heikera L20-24; Bira L24-27; verse split L27-31; challenge and tziva analogy L32-38; 've'eima' begun and left open L39. 'inauguration verse' is supported by Rashi on 2a (Rashi lines 47-49 'bemiluim'). No 2b content is stated.
glossaryEvidence: Parhedrin (L3, Rashi 4 'kakh shemah'); Parah Adumah (L8-14, L18-19, Rashi 13); Tvul Yom (L14-17); Gezerah Shavah (general definition, applied L35-38); Milu'im (Rashi 47-55 on 2a). No claim rests on anything outside 2a.

perSugya.evidence: Mishnah L1-7. Rule, backup kohen, R. Yehuda's proposal and verse, and 'ein ladavar sof' are accurately rendered; the 'replacement wife could also die' gloss is Rashi 11-12 on 2a; 'tamei' is Rashi 7-9.

defects.says: 'Halachic preparation for contingencies is bounded by the practical ability to terminate the chain. A rule that generates infinite new obligations cannot stand.'
defects.sourceSupports: Only that 'they said to him: if so there is no end to the matter' (L7), as one side of an undecided dispute. No general halachic principle is stated, and the same Mishnah (L3-4) does prepare a backup kohen although that chain is equally open-ended, so the generalization is not derivable from these lines.

defects.says: 'Classic Talmudic rejection pattern: ein la'davar sof terminates rules that cannot self-limit.'
defects.sourceSupports: Nothing on the page characterizes the retort as a classic pattern or as a rule that terminates rules; unsupported descriptive claim about the Talmud at large.

perSugya.evidence: L8-14: 'tenan hatam' citation of the seven-day separation of the kohen who burns the parah to the chamber al penei habira, north-east, called Lishkat Beit HaEven; the name question and answer (all its acts in dung, stone, earth vessels) are the Gemara's own words and are attributed to the Gemara. finalRuling restates the cited Mishnah. sourceRefs lines 8 and 13 fall in range.

L14-20: question, tevul yom fit for the parah, detenan proof (made tamei and immersed, against the Sadducees who said 'beme'orvei hashemesh'), Rabbinic institution of non-susceptible vessels so it not be treated lightly: all accurately rendered and correctly sequenced; misconception is sound.

defects.says: The leniency was 'demonstrated publicly' / 'Sages prove it publicly' / 'To publicly demonstrate against the Sadducean rule'.
defects.sourceSupports: 'metamin hayu ... umatbilin oto lehotzi milibban shel tzedukin' only. Neither the Gemara nor Rashi on 2a says the act was public or who witnessed it; 'publicly' is an added fact repeated in four fields.

perSugya.evidence: L20-24: mai shena tzefona mizracha; chatat requires north; 'el nokhach penei ohel moed'; Rabbis instituted a north-east chamber for heikera. Details beyond the Gemara (corner of the azara, chatat slaughtered in north but the parah itself not, east via the Heichal entrance in the eastern wall, the kohen made attentive and careful) are all in Rashi 15-16 and 29-43 on 2a.

L24-27: speakers, chain (Rabba bar bar Chana for R. Yochanan), both positions, the proof verse, and the unresolved status with empty finalRuling are correct. David as speaker of the verse in Chronicles is Rashi 43-46.

defects.says: Reish Lakish treats 'bira' as a 'common noun' / 'category' / 'generic category'; 'Classic dispute between specific toponym vs. generic category in Mishnaic geography'.
defects.sourceSupports: Reish Lakish says 'kol hamikdash kulo karui bira': the whole Temple is called Bira. That is still the name of one specific referent, not a common noun or a category; the page supports only specific place on the Temple Mount versus the entire Mikdash. 'Classic' has no basis on the page.

defects.says: 'I Chronicles 29:19 is part of David's final speech bequeathing the Temple project to Solomon.'
defects.sourceSupports: The page gives only the words 'habira asher hakhinoti'; Rashi says only that David says the verse in Chronicles. The verse is from David's prayer to God (as display.whats itself says: 'David's prayer'), not a speech of bequest; unsupported and internally inconsistent.

perSugya.evidence: L27-38: mena hanei milei; three-link chain to R. Yochanan; verse quoted as worded (Lev 8:34); la'asot = parah, lekhaper = Yom Kippur; bishlama concession and 'say all of it is Yom Kippur'; tziva-tziva with 'zot chukat hatorah asher tziva Hashem lemor' (Num 19:2); 'as there parah so here parah, as here separation so there separation'. Inauguration context is Rashi 47-55. Every field stops at L38 and says only that the discussion continues; no 2b content. finalRuling empty.
